_meta.description: Proposed test-design cases — not executed fixtures or passing results. Begin with one schema-valid eligible effective request and a fixed scope; change only the named input per pair, keep every other dependency constant. Reviewed canonical bytes and digest vectors must be saved once spec/schemas/ is frozen (done, this M0 pass) — never regenerate expected values from the implementation under test merely to make a failing fixture pass.

mutation_pairs.mutation: reorder JSON object properties without changing their values
mutation_pairs.expected_relationship: same canonical bytes and request digest

mutation_pairs.mutation: omit an option versus supply its documented default
mutation_pairs.expected_relationship: same digest after effective-default expansion, where the schema defines equivalence

mutation_pairs.mutation: change only a transport request ID or a secret excluded from the effective request
change message whitespace, case, or content; prompt/schema/normalization version; model; deployment revision; effective generation setting
change application namespace, store instance, history ID, or cache generation
mutation_pairs.expected_relationship: different scope digest and final key

mutation_pairs.mutation: append unrelated history while a content-only summary's complete effective inputs stay identical
mutation_pairs.expected_relationship: same summary request digest and scope — no blanket history-revision invalidation

mutation_pairs.mutation: change tree context actually supplied to routing or classification
supply non-finite numbers, invalid Unicode, or duplicate keys in serialized JSON input

cross_language_check: run M1–M8 in both Python and TypeScript against the same reviewed canonical-bytes/digest vectors once packages/ exist (AT-11, AT-15) — this file records the mutation-pair design now, at M0; the actual saved digest vectors are generated once an implementation exists to compute them against this frozen key formula (spec/cache-format.md).
